purpose: Auditable source research and policy-accepted snapshots for M2.

selected.reason: Golden Farm scenario crop; BARC portal land/soil text corroborated in both languages.
Frontend demo crop; BARC portal land/soil and maturity-indicator text corroborated in both languages.
Frontend demo crop (Corn) and M6 class label; harvest calendar corroborated; no corroborated soil condition.
Main Bangladesh crop and M6 class label; only regional context passes the policies.

initial_crop_coverage.coverage_limitation: Positive farm-level fit is available only for Potato (high land + loam) and Wheat (high or medium-high land + loam or clay loam) anywhere in Bangladesh, as general published conditions. No crop has verified growth-stage definitions, so season plans, initial tasks, and season activation remain unavailable.

review_workflow.production_approval: Four automated source policies accept narrowly defined, machine-checked facts: m2-barc-upazila-zoning-v1 (legacy BARC Potato/Comilla map snapshot), m2-barc-portal-bilingual-v1 (values stated in BOTH the English and Bangla text of the same BARC Agri-Advisory Portal record), m2-barc-portal-variety-duration-v1 (published variety duration within 30-250 days, directly planted crops only), and m2-barc-czs-upazila-suitability-v1 (upazila class distribution, regional context only). Every accepted row expires 180 days after capture. Read-time validation rebuilds each row from the pinned capture and claim manifest; edited rows are ignored.
review_workflow.limitation: No human reviewer is assigned; reviewed_by and reviewed_at stay null. Facts that one language version contradicts, or that only one language states, are not accepted.

sources.document_or_page_title: Land Suitability Assessment and Crop Zoning of Bangladesh — Introduction and methodology
sources.date_note: No publication or dataset version date was visible on the reviewed page.
facts_supported: The page describes suitability assessment using agro-edaphic and agro-climatic inputs.
The page describes suitability classes and states that crop zoning is generated at upazila level.
limitations: Methodology is not itself a potato recommendation for an individual farm.
The page does not provide an effective period for the displayed datasets.
Local recommendation requires the matching verified crop and locality data; no Comilla-local data version was verified for ingestion.

sources.document_or_page_title: Suitability Map of Potato — Bangladesh map
sources.date_note: No publication or dataset version date was visible on the reviewed page.
facts_supported: The page displays Bangladesh-wide potato land-area totals by suitability class.
limitations: National aggregate area totals do not establish suitability for a specific farm, district, or upazila.
No effective date or verified downloadable data snapshot was recorded.

sources.document_or_page_title: Suitability Map of Potato — Comilla upazila
sources.date_note: The map page does not publish an underlying data version. Snapshot captured 2026-10-07; source and methodology response hashes are recorded in barc_potato_comilla_snapshot.json.
facts_supported: The page reports mapped area by Potato suitability class for Comilla upazila.
Very suitable 1645 ha; suitable 11020 ha; moderately suitable 2544 ha; marginally suitable 0 ha; not suitable 5364 ha; total 20573 ha.
limitations: The map reports upazila aggregate area, not field-level suitability.
The map data vintage is not stated; accepted snapshots expire after 180 days.
This evidence does not provide season stages, tasks, or harvest guidance.

The map's 'Comilla' upazila is the pre-split legacy unit; BARC's current suitability API lists Adarsha Sadar, Sadar Dakshin, and Lalmai instead. Without a source-backed mapping the record matches only a farm whose saved upazila is the legacy name 'Comilla', so current-upazila context records supersede it.

sources.organization: Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) — Agri-Advisory Portal
sources.publication_or_update_date: per-record updated_at: potato 2024-01-28, wheat 2025-02-23, maize 2024-01-03, Boro rice 2024-01-01
sources.date_note: Each record names its upstream source (for example Hand Book of Agricultural Technology, 2013, BARI).
sources.reuse_terms: Portal copyright policy: free reproduction in any format without specific permission if reproduced accurately, not in a misleading context, and with the source acknowledged (captured at portal/copyright_policy.html).
facts_supported: Potato: high land with loam soil (both languages).
Wheat: high and medium-high land with loam or clay loam soil (both languages).
Wheat maturity indicator: golden colour (both languages).
Maize harvest calendar: Rabi late March to second week of April; Kharif-1 mid to late June (both languages).
limitations: English and Bangla fields often disagree (potato sowing, irrigation, and harvest timing; maize soils); only corroborated values are accepted. See barc_portal_claims.json rejected_claims.
General Bangladesh advisory, not location- or field-specific.

sources.organization: Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) — Agri-Advisory Portal
sources.document_or_page_title: Crop Variety Information (public JSON routes /api/get-variety-names-by-crop/{id} and /api/get-variety-by-id/{id})
facts_supported: Official variety names for the M1 catalog (245 potato, wheat, maize, Boro and T. Aman rice varieties).
Duration ranges for 112 potato, wheat, and maize varieties.
limitations: The portal does not state the event a duration is counted from; FieldShift counts from the season planting date and says so.
Five records were rejected: four potato varieties publish no duration, and BARI Hybrid Vutta-10 lists an implausible 10-150 days.
The publisher's is_active flag is false on every inspected record and its meaning is undocumented; it is recorded but not used.
Rice durations are not used because the counting basis (seedbed sowing or transplanting) is unstated.

sources.organization: Bangladesh Agricultural Research Council (BARC) — Crop Zoning System, developed by the Institute of Water Modelling
sources.document_or_page_title: Crop Suitability by upazila (public JSON routes on api1.cropzoning.gov.bd used by the portal's cropSuitability page)
facts_supported: 64 districts and 482 upazilas with BBS geocodes (M1 geography reference).
Per-upazila distribution across suitability classes (80-100%, 60-80%, 40-60%, 20-40%, below 20% of attainable yield) by season and crop situation.
limitations: The API does not state the area unit; only unit-free shares are shown.
Upazila aggregates never establish farm-level fit.
Captured for 48 upazilas in 5 districts; other upazilas have no regional context until the capture covers them.

sources.document_or_page_title: Krishi Projukti Hatboi (Handbook on Agro-Technology), 10th edition
sources.date_note: Linked from the official BARI handbook page (page updated 2025-08-28).
limitations: Text uses the legacy SutonnyMJ font encoding; extracted text loses conjuncts, so claims cannot be machine-verified. A Unicode or verified-OCR edition is needed before growth stages or harvest guidance can be extracted.

sources.document_or_page_title: Khamari information materials (booklets 2024 and 2025, flyer 2026, user manual, two articles)
facts_supported: Khamari provides land-specific crop suitability and fertilizer recommendations from a field location.
limitations: The Bangla booklet and flyer use SutonnyMJ encoding.
Field-level Khamari and CZIS results come from role-gated CZIS modules and an undocumented GeoServer; FieldShift does not call or scrape them.

sources.document_or_page_title: Agro-met forecast and BWDB flood warnings
limitations: Forecasts and warnings are time-limited and belong to M4 weather intelligence; they are not stored as permanent M2 knowledge.

sources.document_or_page_title: SRDI portal and upazila land and soil resource guides
facts_supported: Bangladesh land-type classes (high, medium high, medium low, low, very low) used as the M1 land-type vocabulary.
limitations: No upazila soil guide was ingested; plot soil values remain farmer-reported.
Commercial subscription service built on a customer's own field sensors for Canadian farming; it publishes no open Bangladesh data or reuse terms.

candidate_facts: See barc_portal_claims.json for accepted claims, exclusions, and rejected claims.
exclusion_reason: Growth stages, initial tasks, sowing windows, irrigation schedules, and fertilizer doses are not imported: no inspected source states them consistently in a machine-verifiable form.
